label: first input token is a (t=0, in_tok=a)
explanation: Fires at step 0 when the first original token is the letter a, at a nearly constant magnitude (~1.74, the max). It also has a weak secondary activation (~0.12, about 7% of max) at t=1 when the sequence starts "k a". This accounts for the remaining 3% of active steps and 0.2% of mass; adding that clause gives dev F1 1.0. Magnitude does not depend on L or the rest of the sequence. It never fires on a at later positions, on any other token, or in the delimiter or copy phases.

issues: The claims hold. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.969, F1 0.984 and mass recall 0.998. The correlation of 0.9999 confirms a nearly constant magnitude: median and max are both 1.740.

The dev profile backs every 'never fires' claim. The feature is active 0 times in the delimiter and copy phases, 0 times at t>=2, and 0 times on any in_tok other than a. Activation mass is flat across L (about 0.165 per length; L=3 is lower only because it is a smaller bucket).

The only gap that follows a pattern is the secondary 'k a' case the explanation already describes: 573 dev steps at t=1, all in the lowest activation quartile. Test coverage of the first quartile is 0.87 without this clause. Adding the clause ((t==1) & (orig(0)==tok('k')) & (in_tok==tok('a'))) gives test precision, recall, F1 and mass recall of 1.0, so it is exact.
Minor: the label leaves out the weak 'k a' secondary clause. That is acceptable because the clause holds only 0.2% of activation mass and the explanation discloses it.
